note: frozen artifacts only; taxonomy mapping corrected (all-clear = CNN- AND (L2 quiet OR abstain)); TWA = P(presented reliable AND CNN wrong); S6 additionally reports trusted-garbage (any trusted output on faulted audio)
conclusion: S0 (bare CNN) leaves a supervisor misinformed on up to 37.5% of files (hydrhigh no-leak) and 30.2% on tube leaks — and 12-76% of those errors are confident (max-softmax >= 0.9), the case no self-referential monitor can catch.

Single-monitor arms each have a blind spot: MSP helps only moderately (tube TWA 30.2->19.1%), L2-only barely moves TWA because its abstention leaves errors trusted (97-100% of CNN- true leaks stay silent), L3-only is the strongest single monitor (tube TWA -> 8.5%, flatline 58.3->0%).

The full cascade S2 is best on every shifted condition (hydrhigh no-leak 37.5->0%, hydr leak ->2.3-5.0%, tube 30.2->8.3%, dropout/flatline/offset ->0%) but is NOT clean on tube: 48 of 174 CNN- tube files remain all-clear silent misses (120 caught as T4, 4 as T2).

On S6 faulted audio the CNN still reports leak on 25-69% of files (silent garbage) and MSP flags only 1.5-25% of it; only arms containing L1 or L3 suppress this (S2: 0% trusted on all faults except clipping, where L1's known blind spot leaves 63.5% trusted).
Nominal cost: S2 FAR 4.4% on nominal no-leak (driven by the reported mic1 L1 clipping bug: 15% mic1, 0-2.5% others) vs 0% bare CNN and 0% L3-only — supervision is cheap but not free.
